q: Which structure–function pair for the chloroplast is correct?
options: The thylakoid lumen contains Rubisco, so CO2 can be fixed right beside the photosystems
Stroma holds the Calvin cycle enzymes beside the thylakoids, so ATP and NADPH reach them fast
The grana contain all of the Calvin cycle enzymes, which maximises the rate of carbon fixation
The outer membrane holds the photosystems, so they receive the most light possible
explanation: The light-dependent reactions take place on thylakoid membranes, and their products (ATP and NADPH) are released on the stromal side – straight into the stroma, where Rubisco and the other Calvin cycle enzymes are dissolved. Compartments keep enzymes and substrates concentrated, and keep the lumen separate so a proton gradient can form.
